# Embedded Development Environment on xstation

## Identity

- Host: `xstation`
- Capability: embedded / RTOS firmware development workstation
- Workspace root: `/mnt/work` (also reachable via `~/work` symlink)
- Primary OS target: **OpenVela** (Xiaomi NuttX-based RTOS) wearable/SoC firmware
- Login user: `elliot`
- Created record: 2026-05-25

This host is the heavy-lifting build/debug node for several OpenVela `repo`
workspaces plus one Allwinner Linux BSP patch project. Toolchains are vendored
inside each workspace's `prebuilts/`, not installed system-wide.

## Workspace inventory (`/mnt/work`)

| Dir | Type | Target / chip | Source (repo manifest) | Last active |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `new` | OpenVela `repo` workspace (current main) | watch SoC (o63 referenced in aliases) | `ssh://10.166.0.122:29418/manifests.git` (internal Gerrit) | 2026-12 |
| `vela-opensource` | OpenVela public reference | generic / emulator | `ssh://git@gitee.com/open-vela/manifests.git` | 2025-11 |
| `rivotek_trunk5` | OpenVela vendor trunk | Rivotek vendor | `ssh://10.166.0.122:29418/manifests.git` | 2025-11 |
| `p62-dev` | OpenVela `repo` workspace | P62 watch board (BES) | `ssh://git.odm.mioffice.cn:29418/velaos/vendor/manifest` | 2025-09 |
| `miwear_projects` | OpenVela `repo` workspace | Mi Wear (miuiwatch/miwear, BES) | `ssh://git.odm.mioffice.cn:29418/velaos/vendor/manifest` + `ssh://git.mioffice.cn:29418/vela/manifests` | 2025-10 |
| `x4b` | OpenVela superset workspace (partially synced; `.repo` only) | multi-board (allwinner/android/bes-o62/car) | `ssh://git.mioffice.cn:29418/vela/manifests` (+ git.n.xiaomi.com, git.xiaomi.com) | 2025-09 |
| `huaqian_upgrade` | Allwinner Linux BSP patch project (NOT a NuttX repo workspace) | Allwinner **R528** + Tina Linux 5.0 | local tarballs + patch sets | 2025-12 |

Notes:
- All OpenVela workspaces share the same layout: `apps/ nuttx/ frameworks/
  external/ vendor/ prebuilts/ .repo/`, with `build.sh -> nuttx/tools/build.sh`
  and an `emulator.sh -> prebuilts/emulator/tools/emulator.sh`.
- `huaqian_upgrade` is different: it holds the `tina-r528-vela` BSP plus patch
  bundles for MIPI screen flicker, multiple-LCD support, and USB disconnection
  fixes on R528 Tina 5.0. Apply via `do_patch.sh` / `check_src.sh`.
- Board/chip codenames seen across workspaces and configs: `n62`, `p62`, `p65`,
  `o62`, `o63`, `x4b`, `bes-1700`, `bes-o62` — BES (Bestechnic) class smartwatch
  SoCs.
- VS Code multi-root workspaces live in `/mnt/work/workspaces/*.code-workspace`
  (`n62`, `p62`, `p65`, `rivotek_trunk5`, `vela`, `new`).

## Toolchains

Toolchains are bundled per workspace under `prebuilts/`. None are on the global
`PATH` by default; they are resolved relative to the active workspace.

### Vela prebuilts (`/mnt/work/vela-opensource/prebuilts/tools/linux/x86_64`)

- `arm-none-eabi-gcc` — Arm GNU Toolchain 11.3.Rel1 (11.3.1 20220712)
- `riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc` — SiFive GCC-Metal 10.2.0
- `clang` — clang 16.0.0
- helpers: `ccache`, `genromfs`, `aidl`, `hidl-gen`, `amap`
- also `prebuilts/{qemu,emulator,build-tools,clang,gcc}` for host emulation

### Mi Wear prebuilts (`/mnt/work/miwear_projects/prebuilts/gcc/linux`)

- `arm/` — arm-none-eabi-gcc 11.3.Rel1 (+ `arm-none-eabi-gdb`)
- `arm64/`
- `risc-v/`
- `tc32/` — **Telink** `tc32-elf-gcc 4.5.1` (BLE MCU) + bundled `openocd`
- `xtensa/` — BES **HiFi4** DSP toolchain (`hifi4_bes_asic`, `hifi4_bes_fpga`)

### System / user tools

- `gdb` 12.x, `gdb-multiarch` (`/usr/bin`)
- `st-flash`, `st-info` (STM32, `/usr/bin`)
- `dfu-util` (`/usr/bin`)
- `esptool.py` (ESP, `~/.local/bin`)
- `openocd` (from Telink prebuilts, on PATH)
- `qemu-system-arm`, `qemu-system-aarch64` (`/usr/bin`)
- `dtc` 1.4.5 (device tree compiler, `~/dtc`)

text:
核验完成,现在结论清晰了。本地这份 `~/mywork/u-boot` 其实**带着完整的主线历史**(v2025.07、1449 个 defconfig,非 shallow),我之前只匹配到 3 个是因为主线把全志板子按板名命名了(mangopi、licheerv 等)。更关键的是 **`mangopi_mq_r_defconfig` 就是 R528**(`CONFIG_MACH_SUN8I_R528=y`,DT `sun8i-t113s-mangopi-mq-r`)——主线已经原生支持 R528/T113s。

## U-Boot 现状评估

**1. 三棵 Tina BSP 里的 U-Boot —— 全是全志 brandy 老版本**
- `tina5.0-r528`、`T113-Tina5.0` → `brandy/brandy-2.0/u-boot-2018`,版本 **2018.07**
- `tina-r328` → `lichee/brandy-2.0/u-boot-2018`,版本 **2018.05**
- 都是全志深度魔改:私有子系统 `sunxi_flash / sunxi_crypto / sunxi_power / sunxi_usb / sunxi_ir`,`sun8iw20p1_*` defconfig
- 启动链:`BROM → boot0(spl-pub/sboot,含安全启动)→ u-boot-2018 → kernel`,最终由 Tina 的 `tools/pack` 打包成可烧录镜像
- 距主线约 **7 年 / 14 个发布周期**,确实"偏且旧"

**2. 独立的 `~/mywork/u-boot` —— 处于半成品状态**
- git HEAD 还 detached 在一个 **2017.01 的老 Lichee-Pi 提交**上,但工作区被覆盖成了全志 2018.07(相对该 HEAD 有 **9747 个改动文件**)——所以它现在**不是干净的主线基底**
- 但它已经配好官方 `uboot` 远程,且**完整的主线历史都在本地**了(v2025.07,非 shallow)。等于迁移的"料"备齐了,就差正式开工

**3. 主线对你的芯片支持很好(这是好消息)**
- R528 → `mangopi_mq_r_defconfig`(`MACH_SUN8I_R528`),T113-s3 同 die 也覆盖,还有 licheerv_nano 等
- 含义:**不需要把全志 2018.07 整棵移植过来**。正确做法是**以主线为基底,只把你板子真正需要的差异挪过去**(DRAM 参数、你的板级 DT、MIPI 屏、NAND/NOR + env 布局、个别外设驱动)
- 例外:**R328 (sun8iw18) 主线几乎没支持**,是这几个里最难的;R528/T113 最容易

**4. 真正的难点 = 启动/烧录集成**,有两条路:
- **A 保留 Tina 生产流程**:沿用 boot0 + `tools/pack`,只把 u-boot 主阶段换成主线版 → 对 Tina 构建/烧录/安全启动改动最小,但要让主线 u-boot 适配厂商 boot0 的加载地址与交接
- **B 走全主线**:主线 SPL 自己做 DRAM 初始化,用你已有的 **`xfel`(FEL 烧写,udev 规则都在)** 或 SD 卡烧写 → 最干净、最现代,但放弃 Tina 的 pack / 安全启动 / 量产烧录流程

下面两个决定会直接影响怎么开工,定一下方向:

input.title: U-Boot 主线迁移分析
input.summary: 评估 Tina R528/T113 的 brandy u-boot 2018.07 现状,对比主线支持,规划全主线迁移路线

output.text: Chapter marked: "U-Boot 主线迁移分析". Continue your current work.

text:
# R528 vs T113 上主线 —— 对比与落地路线

## 一、对比表

| 维度 | R528 (tina5.0-r528 / evb2) | T113 (T113-Tina5.0 / evb1) |
|---|---|---|
| 芯片 die | sun8iw20p1(Cortex-A7 + C906 RISC-V) | sun8iw20p1(双 Cortex-A7) — **同 die** |
| Tina 现状 | brandy **u-boot 2018.07** | brandy **u-boot 2018.07** |
| **主线起步 defconfig** | `mangopi_mq_r_defconfig`(`MACH_SUN8I_R528`) | **同上**(主线无独立 t113 defconfig) |
| **主线 DT** | `sun8i-t113s-mangopi-mq-r-t113.dts` + `sun8i-t113s.dtsi` | **共用 `sun8i-t113s.dtsi`** |
| DRAM | DDR3 @ 792MHz(`dram_type=3`) | DDR3 @ 792MHz — 同类型 |
| **启动介质** | **SPI-NAND**(`storage_type=5`) | **SPI-NAND**(也有 nor/nand 变体) |
| 主线支持度 | 高(板级直接存在) | 高(随 t113s 家族复用) |

**核心结论**:R528 和 T113-s3 在主线里是**同一个 `sun8i-t113s` 家族**。所以"两个都要"其实**先做 R528 就顺带覆盖了 T113 的 ~90%**——SoC 初始化、DRAM 驱动、SPI/USB/MMC、`t113s.dtsi` 全共用,T113 只剩自己的板级 DT(双核 A7、引脚、外设)和量产介质差异。建议 **R528 先行,T113 跟随**,而不是并行两套。

## 二、各自要从 Tina 搬过去的"板级 delta"(走全主线只搬这些,不搬整棵 2018.07)

- **DRAM 参数**:`sys_config.fex [dram_para]` 的 `dram_clk/type/zq/para1/2/mrX/tprX` → 填进主线 sun20i DRAM 的 Kconfig/板配置(已提取到 R528/evb2 的全套值)
- **板级 DT**:Tina 的 `uboot-board.dts` + `sys_config.fex` 里的 pinmux/外设 → 映射成主线 `.dts`(基于 `sun8i-t113s.dtsi`)
- **env / 分区**:`env.cfg` + `sys_partition.fex` → 主线 env 布局 + 分区(自建,不用 Tina pack)
- **显示/MIPI**(R528 重点,对应 `huaqian_upgrade` 的屏闪/多 LCD 补丁):MIPI-DSI 屏驱动与时序,主线这块要单独适配
- **PMIC/power**:`sunxi_power`(AXP)→ 主线 PMIC 驱动

## 三、B 路线(全主线 + 自建烧录)落地里程碑

1. **FEL/RAM 跑通(xfel,storage 无关)** ← 最快验证:构建主线 `mangopi_mq_r`,xfel 直接加载到内存,验证 SoC + DRAM + 串口控制台。**先证明主线能在你板子上起来**。
2. **SD 卡启动**:主线 SPL 对 SD 支持很稳,第二步落地。
3. **SPI-NAND 启动 ← 头号风险**:主线已有 `drivers/mtd/nand/spi/core.c` + `spi-sunxi.c`,但 **SPL 阶段从 SPI-NAND 引导 sun8iw20 需要实测/可能要 backport**(SD/NOR 没问题,SPI-NAND 是主线 sunxi 的薄弱点)。这步过了,B 路线才算对你的量产介质完整可用。
4. **搬板级 delta + 自建烧录脚本**(xfel/dd/SD),彻底脱离 Tina 的 boot0 + pack。

## 四、两点必须先处理的前置项

- **独立 `~/mywork/u-boot` 工作区是脏的**:HEAD detached 在 2017.01,工作区是厂商 2018.07 覆盖(9747 个未提交改动)。**不要在这棵脏树上直接 checkout 主线**——会冲掉你现有的厂商参考。建议用 `git worktree` 从 `uboot` 远程的 `v2025.07` 拉一棵**干净的主线工作树**(对象都在本地,不下载),厂商 2018.07 树原样保留作对照。
- **R328 不在本次范围**:它是 sun8iw18,主线几乎没支持,是另一档难度——本次只做 R528/T113 是对的。

---

下一步我建议先做**非破坏性的第一步**:用 `git worktree` 建一棵干净的主线树,构建 `mangopi_mq_r` 的 u-boot,确认能编出来(顺带核实 arm-linux-gnueabi 工具链)。这一步**不动你现有的任何东西**。要我现在就做吗?还是你想先看我把 R528/evb2 已提取的整套 DRAM 参数 + 分区/env 映射成主线配置的草稿?
我不需要你给我看草稿，我希望你想一想，就是通过做这些活，你需要哪些，然后你可以并行起很多Agent，嗯，也可以并行去做。新建你的worktree

明白。你要的是:我把这件事拆成能并行的独立工作流,建好各自的 worktree,然后并行派多个 agent 去做。先想清楚需要什么 + 做点前置检查(交叉工具链、worktree 可行性、磁盘),再建 worktree、派活。

## 我做这件事需要的东西

- **干净的主线 u-boot 工作树**(从 `uboot` 远程 `v2025.07`,对象已在本地)——给构建用,且不能碰那棵脏的 2018.07 参考树

- **Tina 侧的输入**(已定位):R528/evb2 与 T113/evb1 的 `sys_config.fex`(DRAM/pinmux)、`uboot-board.dts`、`env.cfg`、`sys_partition.fex`

input.prompt:
You are helping migrate an Allwinner R528 board from a vendor U-Boot 2018.07 (Allwinner Tina SDK "brandy") to mainline U-Boot v2025.07. Your job: get mainline U-Boot building for the R528 and produce a FEL-loadable image, then document exactly how. This is build + documentation only — NO hardware is attached, so do not attempt to flash or run on a device.

ENVIRONMENT
- Platform: Ubuntu 22.04 x86_64, shell bash. You have sudo but do NOT install system packages unless truly unavoidable (and if so, report it rather than assuming).
- A clean mainline U-Boot v2025.07 git worktree is already checked out for you at:
  /home/elliot/mywork/uboot-wt/r528   (branch: mainline-r528, commit "Prepare v2025.07")
  Work IN this directory. Do not touch /home/elliot/mywork/u-boot (a separate dirty tree).
- Target SoC: Allwinner R528 = sun8iw20 family. The mainline starting defconfig is `mangopi_mq_r_defconfig` (CONFIG_MACH_SUN8I_R528=y, device tree sun8i-t113s-mangopi-mq-r-t113). The boot core is ARM Cortex-A7 (32-bit ARM build).

TOOLCHAIN (important — there is NO arm-linux-gnueabi/hf gcc on this system)
- Available: arm-none-eabi-gcc 11.3 at /home/elliot/work/vela-opensource/prebuilts/tools/linux/x86_64/arm-none-eabi-gcc (add that dir to PATH). U-Boot is freestanding so `CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi-` usually works for sunxi ARM. Try this first.
- Fallback A: search the Tina SDK for a bundled linaro toolchain: `find /home/elliot/mywork/tina5.0-r528 -name 'arm-linux-gnueabi*-gcc' 2>/dev/null` and the .buildconfig references `gcc-linaro-5.3.1-2016.05-x86_64_arm-linux-gnueabi`.
- Fallback B (last resort, report don't auto-install): `sudo apt-get install gcc-arm-linux-gnueabihf`.
- A device tree compiler is available at /home/elliot/dtc (dtc 1.4.5) and the u-boot tree ships scripts/dtc; system needs python3 (present), swig/libssl may be needed for some host tools — work around if possible.

TASKS
1. Build: `cd /home/elliot/mywork/uboot-wt/r528 && make mangopi_mq_r_defconfig && make -j$(nproc) CROSS_COMPILE=...`. Resolve build errors pragmatically. Capture which toolchain + exact commands worked.
2. Identify the produced artifacts (especially `u-boot-sunxi-with-spl.bin`, `spl/sunxi-spl.bin`, `u-boot.bin`, `u-boot.dtb`), their paths and sizes.
3. Research and write down the correct FEL bring-up command sequence for R528/sun8iw20 using `xfel` (RAM load: ddr init, write u-boot-sunxi-with-spl.bin to the right SRAM/DRAM address, exec) — for the user to run later when the board is attached. Look at xfel docs/source at /home/elliot/mywork/xfel if helpful. State the load address and any R528-specific notes.
4. Note anything the default mangopi_mq_r config assumes that may differ for a custom R528 board (DRAM params, console UART, storage) — but do NOT try to fix the board port; just flag handoffs to the DRAM/DT workstreams.

OUTPUT
- Write a concise markdown report to /home/elliot/mywork/uboot-wt/_reports/01-build-r528.md (toolchain used, exact build commands, artifacts table, FEL command sequence, build warnings/risks).
- Then return a summary under 250 words: did it build, with which toolchain, artifact paths, the FEL command, and any blockers.

You are helping migrate an Allwinner R528 board (Tina SDK "evb2" board) from vendor U-Boot 2018.07 to mainline U-Boot v2025.07. Your job (read-only research, no builds): produce a device-tree / board port plan — what the vendor board uses vs what mainline already provides, and the concrete delta to add for this board.

VENDOR INPUTS (R528/evb2)
- Board DT: /home/elliot/mywork/tina5.0-r528/device/config/chips/r528/configs/evb2/uboot-board.dts
- Pinmux + peripheral config (INI-style): /home/elliot/mywork/tina5.0-r528/device/config/chips/r528/configs/evb2/sys_config.fex
  In sys_config.fex, the [uart*], [twi*]/[i2c*], [spi*], [nand0_para]/[spinor_para], [sdc*], [usbc*], [pmu*]/[power], and any [lcd*]/[dsi*]/[disp] sections describe which peripherals/pins the board uses. The board boots from SPI-NAND (storage_type=5).

MAINLINE REFERENCE (read-only worktree, v2025.07)
- /home/elliot/mywork/uboot-wt/ref
- Relevant DTs: arch/arm/dts/sun8i-t113s.dtsi (the SoC dtsi — mainline treats R528 and T113-s3 as the same t113s family) and arch/arm/dts/sun8i-t113s-mangopi-mq-r-t113.dts (the reference R528 board). Read both.

DELIVERABLE
- A peripheral-by-peripheral comparison: console UART, MMC/SD, SPI + SPI-NAND, USB (host/OTG), I2C, PMIC, and display/MIPI-DSI if the evb2 board uses a panel.
- For each: is it already enabled in sun8i-t113s.dtsi / the mangopi DT? What pins does evb2 use (from sys_config.fex)? What node/pinmux changes are needed to make a mainline DT for evb2?
- Produce the concrete list of DT nodes to add/override for an `sun8i-r528-evb2`-style board DTS based on the mangopi reference.
- Briefly note how T113 (T113-Tina5.0 evb1) would differ (same family; mention if its peripherals/pins differ).

OUTPUT
- Write the plan to /home/elliot/mywork/uboot-wt/_reports/03-dt-delta.md.
- Return a summary under 250 words: which peripherals mainline already covers, which need board DT work, and the highest-effort items (likely MIPI-DSI panel and SPI-NAND).

input.description: Mainline SPL SPI-NAND boot feasibility
input.prompt:
You are de-risking a U-Boot migration. The Allwinner R528 and T113 boards (sun8iw20 / sun20i family) we are moving to mainline U-Boot v2025.07 both BOOT FROM SPI-NAND (the vendor sys_config has storage_type=5 = spinand). The chosen path is "full mainline" (mainline SPL does DRAM init, no vendor boot0), flashing via FEL/xfel or SD. The #1 risk is: can mainline U-Boot's SPL boot directly from SPI-NAND on this SoC family? Answer this concretely.

WHAT TO INVESTIGATE
1. Mainline source (read-only worktree at /home/elliot/mywork/uboot-wt/ref, v2025.07):
   - SPL boot-source support: common/spl/spl_spi.c, common/spl/spl_nand.c, and how sunxi SPL selects boot device (arch/arm/mach-sunxi/, board/sunxi/board.c spl_boot_device()).
   - SPI driver: drivers/spi/spi-sunxi.c. SPI-NAND framework: drivers/mtd/nand/spi/core.c.
   - Kconfig symbols: SPL_SPI, SPL_SPI_LOAD, SPL_SPINAND_SUPPORT / SPL_SPI_NAND, SPL_NAND_SUPPORT, MTD_SPI_NAND, CONFIG_SPL_SPI_SUNXI. Determine which exist and whether sunxi SPL wires SPI-NAND as a boot source. Check `grep -rn 'spinand\|SPI_NAND\|SPL_SPI' /home/elliot/mywork/uboot-wt/ref/arch/arm/mach-sunxi /home/elliot/mywork/uboot-wt/ref/drivers/spi/spi-sunxi.c`.
   - Check whether any mainline sunxi defconfig boots from SPI-NAND (grep configs for SPINAND).
2. Web research (use web search): current state (2023–2025) of mainline U-Boot sunxi SPL SPI-NAND boot for Allwinner D1 / T113 / R528 (sun8iw20). Are there merged patches, out-of-tree patches, or known-good board defconfigs? Note linux-sunxi community status. Cite sources.

DELIVERABLE — a clear verdict:
- Is mainline SPL SPI-NAND boot for sun8iw20: (a) supported out of the box, (b) partially / needs specific Kconfig, or (c) not supported / needs backporting? 
- If config needed: the exact Kconfig symbols and any board glue.
- A recommended fallback/sequencing plan: bring up via FEL (xfel RAM load) first (storage-independent), then SD card (well supported), then tackle SPI-NAND boot last — and what the SPI-NAND step concretely requires.

OUTPUT
- Write findings to /home/elliot/mywork/uboot-wt/_reports/04-spinand.md (with source citations/URLs).
- Return a summary under 250 words with the verdict and the concrete config/backport needed.

input.prompt:
You are preparing the flashing/bring-up tooling for a U-Boot migration on Allwinner R528 and T113 (sun8iw20 / sun20i family). We will flash mainline U-Boot via FEL using `xfel`. Your job: make sure xfel is built and usable, confirm it supports these SoCs, and document the exact FEL command recipes. NO hardware is attached right now, so you cannot run against a real device — build + document only.

ENVIRONMENT
- Ubuntu 22.04 x86_64, bash. The xfel source is at /home/elliot/mywork/xfel (cloned from github.com/xboot/xfel). It ships a udev rule 99-xfel.rules.

TASKS
1. Build xfel: inspect /home/elliot/mywork/xfel (Makefile, README), check if an `xfel` binary already exists; if not, build it (`make`), resolving deps (it needs libusb-1.0 dev headers — if missing, report rather than assuming a sudo install, but check `pkg-config --exists libusb-1.0` first). Report the resulting binary path and `xfel version`/help output.
2. Confirm SoC support: determine whether xfel supports R528 and T113 (sun8iw20). Read the chip support list in the source (e.g. files under src/chips or a chips table) and/or `xfel` help. List the matching chip entries and their DRAM/FEL details.
3. Document the FEL recipes (commands, not execution):
   - RAM bring-up: initialize DRAM (`xfel ddr <type>` — find the correct type/arg for R528/T113), load `u-boot-sunxi-with-spl.bin` to the proper address, and `xfel exec`. Give the exact addresses.
   - Writing to storage via FEL where supported (SPI-NAND `xfel spinand ...`, SPI-NOR `xfel spinor ...`, or SD). State which of these xfel actually supports for this family.
4. udev rule: report whether 99-xfel.rules is installed under /etc/udev/rules.d/ (check), and the command to install it for non-root USB access (don't install without noting it's a system change).

OUTPUT
- Write the recipes + support matrix to /home/elliot/mywork/uboot-wt/_reports/05-xfel.md.
- Return a summary under 250 words: xfel binary path + version, whether R528/T113 are supported, the RAM-load command sequence, which storage-write modes xfel supports for this family, and any build/udev blockers.

output.text:
Report written to `/home/elliot/mywork/uboot-wt/_reports/02-dram-map.md`.

## Summary

**How mainline takes DRAM params for R528/T113:** Both SoCs use `CONFIG_MACH_SUN8I_R528` (same die family — even the "T113s" mangopi board selects it), which pulls in the driver `drivers/ram/sunxi/dram_sun20i_d1.c`. Crucially, that driver's `dram_para_t` struct is **almost entirely hardcoded** in a `static const para` initializer. It does NOT consume the full vendor `[dram_para]` blob. Most timings are **computed** at runtime from `dram_clk` via `ns_to_t()` (DRAMTMG1/2), and MR0/MR2/MR3 + para1/para2 are hardcoded/auto-detected. Only ~7 values are settable via Kconfig.

**The CONFIG_* symbols to set:**
- `CONFIG_DRAM_CLK=792` (no R528 default in Kconfig — must set explicitly)
- `CONFIG_SUNXI_DRAM_TYPE_DDR3=y`
- `CONFIG_DRAM_ZQ=8092667` (int/decimal = 0x7b7bfb)
- `CONFIG_DRAM_SUNXI_ODT_EN=0x0`
- `CONFIG_DRAM_SUNXI_TPR0=0x004a2195`
- `CONFIG_DRAM_SUNXI_TPR11`, `CONFIG_DRAM_SUNXI_TPR12`
- `CONFIG_DRAM_SUNXI_TPR13=0x34000100`

**R528 vs T113 identical?** Nearly. The only Kconfig-settable deltas are TPR11 and TPR12: R528/evb2 = `0x450000`/`0x34`; T113/evb1 = `0x340000`/`0x46`. All five other values are the same. The T113/evb1 profile is byte-for-byte upstream `mangopi_mq_r_defconfig`.

**One field with no mainline equivalent that matters:** R528/evb2 vendor sets `dram_tpr4=0x2000` (enables address muxing in `mctl_com_init`), but mainline forces tpr4=0 with no CONFIG to override it. T113/evb1 has tpr4=0 so it is unaffected. If R528 fails to train, this is the prime suspect and would need a code change, not just a defconfig value. Other vendor fields (tpr1/2/3/7, MR0/2/3) are either recomputed, unused, or coincidentally match mainline's hardcoded constants.

## Summary

**Mainline already covers (just enable + pinctrl):** Mainline treats R528 as the T113-s family, so `sun8i-t113s.dtsi` (via `sunxi-d1s-t113.dtsi`) already contains every controller node — uart0-5, i2c0-3, mmc0-2, spi0/1, usb_otg+ehci/ohci, full DSI/TCON/DE display pipeline, emac — all `status=disabled`. `CONFIG_MACH_SUN8I_R528` and `mangopi_mq_r_defconfig` exist. **USB** and **regulators/PMIC** are essentially copy-paste from the MangoPi MQ-R reference (evb2 has no AXP PMIC — fixed regulators + gpio-charger, same as MangoPi).

**Needs board DT work:**
- **Console:** evb2 uses UART0 on PF2/PF4 (vs MangoPi UART3/PB6-7). Must add a `uart0_pf_pins` group (none exists in the SoC dtsi — PF is claimed by mmc0) and set `CONS_INDEX=1`.
- **SPI-NAND (boot device):** evb2 boots SPI-NAND on PC2-PC7 (quad). spi0 node exists but the SoC pin group is only PC2-PC5 — needs a widened group, a `spi-nand@0` child, MTD/UBI partitions, and SPL boot-source changes.

**Highest-effort items:**
1. **SPI-NAND** — no mainline T113/D1 board uses spi-nand, and SPL SPI-NAND boot for sun20i is uncertain (sunxi SPL historically targets SPI-NOR); this is the real risk.
2. **Display** — evb2's panel is parallel RGB (not DSI). Mainline U-Boot has *no* sun20i display driver at all, so display is Linux-only and should be omitted from the U-Boot DT.

I also flagged that DRAM TPR values must be copied from evb2's FEX (DDR3-792, slightly different from MangoPi's), and noted the PF console-vs-mmc0 pin conflict. T113 evb1 would be a sibling fragment: same SoC, swap DRAM params + storage child/SPL boot source + console UART/pins.

## VERDICT: (c) NOT supported in mainline v2025.07 — needs backporting

Mainline sunxi SPL can boot from SD/eMMC, SPI-NOR, raw parallel NAND, and FEL, but **not SPI-NAND**.

**Source evidence (v2025.07, confirmed `git describe = v2025.07`):**
- `arch/arm/mach-sunxi/spl_spi_sunxi.c` is NOR-only: it issues just the linear `0x03` Read command — no SPI-NAND page-read/cache-read, ECC, or bad-block handling.
- `common/spl/spl_spi.c` uses the SPI-NOR `spi_flash_*` stack; `drivers/mtd/nand/raw/sunxi_nand_spl.c` is the *parallel* NFC controller, not SPI-NAND.
- The SPI-NAND framework (`drivers/mtd/nand/spi/core.c`) is U-Boot-proper only (`obj-$(CONFIG_MTD_SPI_NAND)`, no SPL variant) and needs `SPI_MEM` — but `spi-sunxi.c` has no `.mem_ops` and nothing sunxi selects `SPI_MEM`.
- Symbols `SPL_SPINAND_SUPPORT`, `SPL_SPI_NAND`, `SPL_MTD_SPI_NAND` **do not exist**; `BOOT_DEVICE_SPINAND` exists only for TI K3. **Zero sunxi defconfigs** reference SPINAND. The only R528/T113 board, `mangopi_mq_r_defconfig`, is a minimal SD/FEL config.

**Community status:** The dedicated RFC "Support SPI NAND booting on the T113" (John Watts, 15 patches, Apr 2024 — adds `BOOT_DEVICE_SPINAND`/`SPL_SPINAND`, extends `spl_spi_sunxi.c`) was **orphaned by its author in Jul 2024 and never merged**. Official U-Boot sunxi docs list SPI-NOR only.

**Backport required:** SPL SPI-NAND page reader (port the Watts RFC + smaeul `d1-wip`), a `BOOT_DEVICE_SPINAND` method with the correct BROM `boot_media` mapping, new `SPL_SPINAND*` Kconfig, and a consistent page-layout choice (BSP super-page vs mainline physical).

**Sequencing:** 1) FEL/xfel RAM load (storage-independent — validate DRAM init); 2) SD boot (mature, ship here if schedule is tight); 3) SPI-NAND boot last, as a backporting project — flash/test via `xfel spinand`.

5 个 agent 全部完成。汇总如下(详细报告在 `~/mywork/uboot-wt/_reports/01–05`):

## 结果汇总

**✅ 已经能跑的**
- **主线 v2025.07 对 R528 当场编译通过**:`mangopi_mq_r_defconfig` + `arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.4`(`CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi-`),产出 `u-boot-sunxi-with-spl.bin`(480KB,SPL 带合法 `eGON.BT0` 头)。两个 host 依赖(swig、gnutls)已绕过未装系统包。
- **xfel v1.3.3 已构建,原生支持 R528/T113**(sun8iw20,FEL ID 0x00185900,DDR3)。RAM 加载命令链已就绪:`xfel ddr t113-s3 → write 0x40000000 → exec`。
- **DRAM 基本可控**:T113/evb1 的 DRAM 参数**与上游 mangopi 逐字节相同**;R528/evb2 只需设 `CONFIG_DRAM_CLK=792` 等 ~7 个值,两者仅 TPR11/TPR12 有差异。

**⚠️ 三个 agent 不约而同指向的同一个头号风险 —— SPI-NAND 启动**
- 两块默认板都从 **SPI-NAND** 启动,而**主线 v2025.07 的 SPL 不支持 SPI-NAND 引导**(只支持 SD/eMMC/SPI-NOR/裸 NAND/FEL)。
- 唯一的上游尝试(John Watts 的 15 patch RFC,2024.04)**已被作者弃坑、从未合并**。要走全主线 SPL,这是一个**需要 backport 的子项目**。

**🟡 需要板级适配的点(非阻塞)**
- **控制台**:evb2 用 UART0(PF2/PF4),mangopi 是 UART3;且 PF 口与 mmc0 冲突,要新建 pin group。
- **R528 DRAM 隐患**:evb2 厂商设了 `dram_tpr4=0x2000`(地址复用),主线强制为 0 且无 override——R528 若训练失败,这是首要嫌疑,要改代码(T113 无此问题)。
- **显示**:evb2 是并行 RGB 屏,**主线 u-boot 根本没有 sun20i 显示驱动**——所以显示/MIPI(对应 `huaqian_upgrade` 那些屏补丁)是 **Linux 内核侧的事,不属于 u-boot 迁移范围**,u-boot DT 里直接省掉。

## 由此明确的落地次序

1. **FEL/RAM 跑通**(已具备条件,接上板子即可):验证 DRAM + 控制台 —— 与存储无关,最快见效
2. **SD 卡启动**:主线成熟,"如果排期紧可以先交付在这一档"
3. **SPI-NAND 启动**:backport 项目(Watts RFC + smaeul d1-wip),放最后

这里有个**因新证据需要你拍板的方向**:既然主线 SPL 短期内做不了 SPI-NAND,而你的量产介质就是 SPI-NAND——

你要我把前两个讲透,我把它们拆开说清楚——顺便点明一个关键关系:**这两个其实不是平级的二选一**。第 1 个是"先做最稳的那部分",第 2 个是最终架构之一。

## 选项 1:先 FEL/SD 跑通,SPI-NAND 后定

这是一个**分阶段**策略,不是最终方案。先把跟 SPI-NAND 完全无关的部分做掉:

- **阶段 1a — FEL/内存启动**:构建已完成。接上板子后 `xfel ddr → write 0x40000000 → exec`,U-Boot 整个跑在 DRAM 里,**完全不碰存储**。这一步验证三件事:DRAM 参数(尤其 R528 那个 `tpr4=0x2000` 隐患)、控制台 UART、CPU/时钟。串口能出 U-Boot 提示符,就说明 SoC 移植根上是通的。
- **阶段 1b — SD 卡启动**:主线 SPL **开箱支持 SD/MMC**。把 `u-boot-sunxi-with-spl.bin` 写到 SD 卡 8KB 偏移启动即可,得到一个完整可用的开发启动链(能加载内核等),**零 backport**。

**特点**:风险最低、见效最快,且能在真机上先搞清楚 DRAM/控制台要不要修,再决定要不要投入难的部分。**代价**:它把"量产介质 SPI-NAND"这个决定**往后推**——你最终还是要在选项 2 / 选项 3(混合)里挑一个,只是那时是拿真机结果决策,不是拍脑袋。

## 选项 2:全主线 + backport SPI-NAND SPL

这是**承诺走 100% 主线启动链**(BROM → 主线 SPL → 主线 U-Boot),并自己把"从 SPI-NAND 启动"这个能力补进主线 SPL。具体要干的活(来自 spinand agent 的勘察):

两个问题都查实了。

## 1) 本机 U-Boot 总共 7 棵,本质是「两个世界」

| 路径 | 版本 | 分支 |
|---|---|---|
| `~/mywork/u-boot`(working tree) | **v2018.07** | 厂商源覆盖在 Lichee 历史上;但其 `uboot` 远程是官方主线,是下面 3 棵 worktree 的母库 |
| `uboot-wt/ref` | **v2025.07** | 只读主线参考 |
| `uboot-wt/r528` | **v2025.07** | R528 主线构建 |
| `uboot-wt/spinand` | **v2025.07** | SPI-NAND SPL backport |
| `tina5.0-r528/.../u-boot-2018` | **v2018.07** | R528 厂商 |
| `T113-Tina5.0/.../u-boot-2018` | **v2018.07** | T113 厂商 |
| `tina-r328/.../u-boot-2018` | **v2018.05** | R328 厂商(最老) |

> 去重看就是**两套代码**:厂商 brandy **2018.07**(4 棵)vs 官方主线 **v2025.07**(3 棵 worktree)。xboot/xfel 是另外的引导器/工具,不算 u-boot。

## 2) 主线对全志的支持 —— 你清单上的 5 颗芯片**全都已经在主线里了**

主线 v2025.07 全志家族(`MACH_SUN*`):sun4i(A10)、sun5i、sun6i、sun7i(A20)、sun8i(A23/A33/A83T/**H3**/R40/**V3s**/**R528**)、suniv(**F1C100s/F1C200s**)、sun9i、sun50i(A64/H5/H6/H616/A133)、sun20i(D1/T113)。共 **70 个 defconfig、~157 个 DT**。

| 芯片 | 主线 MACH | 现成 defconfig | DT |
|---|---|---|---|
| **V3s** | `MACH_SUN8I_V3S` | `LicheePi_Zero`、`pinecube` | sun8i-v3s-licheepi-zero、anbernic-rg-nano |
| **H3** | `MACH_SUN8I_H3` | `nanopi_*`、`orangepi_*`、bananapi(数十个) | sun8i-h3-* |
| **F1C100s/F1C200s** | `MACH_SUNIV` | `licheepi_nano`、`lctech_pi_f1c200s` | suniv-f1c100s-licheepi-nano、suniv-f1c200s-lctech-pi/popstick |
| **T113** | `MACH_SUN8I_R528`(t113s) | `mangopi_mq_r` | sun8i-t113s-* |
| **R528** | `MACH_SUN8I_R528` | `mangopi_mq_r` | (同 t113s 家族) |

## 关键结论(对你这件事很重要)

**你要的芯片,主线在 SoC 层面全支持了。** 所以这不是"加芯片支持"的活,而是"**加你的板子**"的活——每颗芯片需要的是:板级 DT + DRAM 参数 + 控制台 + 启动介质。SoC 的重活(时钟、DRAM 驱动、pinctrl、SPL)主线都给了,跟我们正在走的 R528 路子**一模一样**。

而且有个**额外的好消息**:我们做的 **SPI-NAND SPL backport 改的是 `spl_spi_sunxi.c`——全志所有芯片共享的那个文件**。也就是说这块工作**对 V3s / H3 / F1C200s / T113 / R528 全部生效**,不只是 R528/T113。

所以整件事现在可以重新定义成:**一棵以主线 v2025.07 为基底、支持你这个芯片家族(V3s/H3/F1C200s/T113/R528)的统一 U-Boot;主线给 SoC,你贡献板子 + 共享的 SPI-NAND SPL 增强。**

---

按你刚才"可以可以"批准的,我现在并行做两件事:① **派 agent 组装 evb2(R528)首个完整目标**(DRAM+UART0+SPI-NAND DT 合一,基于含 SPI-NAND 的分支);② **在 `~/.sshopt` 建项目记录**(把芯片清单也写进去)。

# U-Boot Mainline Migration (Allwinner) on xstation

## Identity

- Host: `xstation`
- Project: migrate Allwinner boards from vendor U-Boot 2018.07 (Tina SDK
  "brandy") to **mainline U-Boot v2025.07**, full-mainline boot chain, flashed
  via FEL (`xfel`) / SD.
- Working area: `~/mywork/uboot-wt/` (git worktrees off `~/mywork/u-boot`)
- Reports: `~/mywork/uboot-wt/_reports/01..` (markdown, per workstream)
- Created record: 2026-05-25

## Goal / target chip set

Build one mainline-based U-Boot covering this Allwinner family. Mainline already
supports every SoC below; the per-target work is board DT + DRAM params +
console + boot media (NOT adding SoC support).

| Chip | Mainline MACH | Example defconfig | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| V3s | `MACH_SUN8I_V3S` | `LicheePi_Zero`, `pinecube` | sun8i, DDR |
| H3 | `MACH_SUN8I_H3` | `orangepi_*`, `nanopi_*` | broad upstream support |
| F1C100s/F1C200s | `MACH_SUNIV` | `licheepi_nano`, `lctech_pi_f1c200s` | suniv, ARM926, tiny RAM |
| T113 | `MACH_SUN8I_R528` (t113s) | `mangopi_mq_r` | sun8iw20, dual A7 |
| R528 | `MACH_SUN8I_R528` | `mangopi_mq_r` | sun8iw20, A7 + C906; same die as T113-s3 |

Mainline v2025.07 sunxi scope overall: ~70 defconfigs, ~157 DTs, families
sun4i/5i/6i/7i/8i/9i/suniv/sun50i/sun20i.

## U-Boot trees on this host (inventory)

Two real codebases: vendor brandy 2018.07 vs mainline v2025.07.

| Path | Version | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `~/mywork/u-boot` | v2018.07 (working tree) | Lichee-Pi clone; vendor 2018.07 overlaid on a 2017.01 detached HEAD (9747 dirty files). Has remote `uboot` = official mainline (full history, v2025.07). Parent repo of the worktrees below. |
| `~/mywork/uboot-wt/ref` | v2025.07 | read-only mainline reference |
| `~/mywork/uboot-wt/r528` | v2025.07 | branch `mainline-r528` — R528 build |
| `~/mywork/uboot-wt/spinand` | v2025.07 | branch `mainline-spinand` — SPI-NAND SPL backport |
| `~/mywork/tina5.0-r528/brandy/brandy-2.0/u-boot-2018` | v2018.07 | R528 vendor |
| `~/mywork/T113-Tina5.0-V1.2/brandy/brandy-2.0/u-boot-2018` | v2018.07 | T113 vendor |
| `~/mywork/tina-r328/lichee/brandy-2.0/u-boot-2018` | v2018.05 | R328 vendor (oldest) |

Related (not U-Boot): `~/mywork/xboot` (XBOOT), `~/mywork/xfel` (FEL flasher).

## Build environment

- Toolchain: `arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.4` at
  `/home/elliot/work/vela-opensource/prebuilts/gcc/linux-x86_64/arm-none-eabi/bin`
  (PATH), `CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi-`. No `arm-linux-gnueabihf` on system.
- Host build needs `swig` for binman/pylibfdt — currently worked around with a
  download-only swig in a temp dir + `SWIG_LIB`; for a permanent setup
  `sudo apt-get install swig libgnutls28-dev` (system change, not yet done).
- `mkeficapsule` disabled (`CONFIG_TOOLS_MKEFICAPSULE=n`) to avoid gnutls dep.

## Status (2026-05-25)

Done (non-hardware; all verified on disk):

- Mainline v2025.07 **builds for R528** (`mangopi_mq_r_defconfig`); artifacts
  `u-boot-sunxi-with-spl.bin` (~480 KB), `spl/sunxi-spl.bin` (valid `eGON.BT0`).
- **DRAM mapping** (report 02): T113/evb1 == upstream mangopi byte-for-byte;
  R528/evb2 = DDR3@792 via `CONFIG_DRAM_CLK=792` + DDR3 + ZQ `0x7b7bfb` +
  TPR0/11/12/13. Watch-item: R528/evb2 vendor sets `dram_tpr4=0x2000` (address
  muxing) which mainline forces to 0 with no override — prime suspect if R528
  DRAM training fails (would need a code change).
- **Board DT delta** (report 03): mainline `sun8i-t113s.dtsi` already has all
  controllers (disabled). evb2 needs: UART0 console on PF2/PF4 (`CONS_INDEX=1`;
  PF pin group conflicts with mmc0), SPI-NAND on PC2–PC7 (widen pin group + add
  `spi-nand@0` + MTD/UBI). Display on evb2 is **parallel RGB**, and mainline
  U-Boot has **no sun20i display driver** → display is Linux-only, omit from the
  U-Boot DT.
- **SPI-NAND SPL backport** (report 06): branch `mainline-spinand`, 2 commits
  (`596b1820` Kconfig `SPL_SPI_SUNXI_NAND` + `BOOT_DEVICE_SPINAND`;
  `9602fa40` SPI-NAND page-read in `spl_spi_sunxi.c`). Compiles, boot path
  linked. **Re-implemented from the JEDEC SPI-NAND sequence** (the orphaned
  John Watts 2024 RFC patch bodies couldn't be reproduced verbatim; smaeul
  `d1-wip` did not carry the code). Because it edits the shared
  `spl_spi_sunxi.c`, it benefits **all sunxi SoCs**, not just R528/T113.
- **xfel v1.3.3** built (`~/mywork/xfel/xfel`), supports R528/T113 (sun8iw20,
  FEL id `0x00185900`, DDR3), SPI-NOR + SPI-NAND writes. No SD/MMC write in xfel.
  `99-xfel.rules` not yet installed in `/etc/udev/rules.d/`.

Blocked on hardware (no FEL device attached at record time):

- FEL RAM bring-up, SD boot, and SPI-NAND on-target validation all need the
  board connected. The SPI-NAND read correctness (timings, ECC, page size,
  BROM boot-media value, page layout) is **unverified** until then. Page-layout
  choice so far: mainline physical layout, 2 KiB pages, on-die ECC — flash with
  `xfel spinand` (NOT the BSP super-page layout).

## Reference FEL bring-up (when a board is attached)

```bash
# in a built worktree, e.g. ~/mywork/uboot-wt/r528
xfel ddr t113-s3                 # or r528-s3 / t113-s4 (DDR3 presets)
xfel write 0x40000000 u-boot-sunxi-with-spl.bin
xfel exec  0x40000000
# SPI-NAND program (after backport validated):
xfel spinand write 0 u-boot-sunxi-with-spl.bin
```

## Roadmap

```
Phase 0  analysis + worktrees + mainline build + SPI-NAND SPL backport   DONE (non-hw)
Phase 1  on-board FEL RAM boot -> SD boot                                 BLOCKED on hardware
Phase 2  SPI-NAND on-target validation (uses DRAM proven in Phase 1)      BLOCKED on hardware
Per-board roll-out: R528(evb2) -> T113 -> V3s -> H3 -> F1C200s            board DT + DRAM each
```

## Next steps

- Assemble a per-board target (first: `sun8i-r528-evb2`) = mangopi base +
  evb2 DRAM + UART0 console + SPI-NAND DT, branched off `mainline-spinand`,
  built to a flash-ready image.
- When hardware is available: install `99-xfel.rules`, run the FEL sequence,
  validate DRAM (esp. tpr4), then SD, then SPI-NAND.
- Optional: make the swig/gnutls build deps permanent for reproducible builds.

## Notes

- Do not run mainline checkouts in `~/mywork/u-boot` itself (dirty vendor tree);
  use worktrees under `~/mywork/uboot-wt/`.
- R328 (sun8iw18) is essentially unsupported in mainline — out of scope here.

You are assembling the first complete per-board target for a mainline U-Boot v2025.07 port of an Allwinner R528 board (the Tina SDK "evb2" board). Goal: produce a board-specific, flash-ready mainline U-Boot that combines (a) the already-done SPI-NAND SPL backport, (b) evb2 DRAM parameters, (c) evb2 console on UART0, and (d) an evb2 device tree with SPI-NAND. ## Summary

All three vendor trees (R528 + T113 = sun8iw20p1, identical; R328 = sun8iw19) share the same Tina framework. License is good news: the display, NAND-physical, EMAC and sprite/USB code is all GPL-2.0 Allwinner source, not blobs. The blobs are confined to the SPL and the writable-NAND FTL.

Top vendor-only assets worth porting:

1. **Display stack** — `drivers/video/sunxi/disp2/` (biggest asset). The high-value pieces are the **TCON + MIPI-DSI register driver** (`disp/de/lowlevel_v35x/tcon/de_lcd.c`, `de_dsi.c`) and ~60 **panel drivers** (`disp/de/.../lcd/`). Verdict YELLOW: clean GPL C, but everything calls the U-Boot/FEX glue in `disp/disp_sys_intf.c` — port that shim to mainline DM (gpio/pwm/regulator/DT) once, then TCON/DE/panels follow. Panels themselves are near-mechanical to lift (GREEN).

2. **SPI-NAND** — split it: the **physical layer** (chip detect, page read, ECC, BBT) is real GPL C in `drivers/sunxi_flash/.../spinand/` and the cleaner `drivers/mtd/awnand/spinand/physic/`. Verdict GREEN/YELLOW — sufficient for an SPL read path. But the **NFTL** (`nftl.S`, 25k-line asm) is an obfuscated blob — RED, do not copy; use UBI/MTD instead. The first-stage SPL itself ships only as `.a` libs in `spl-pub/board/{r528,t113}/` — RED.

3. **EMAC/GMAC** — `drivers/net/sunxi_gmac.c` (what R528/T113 nand defconfigs enable) and `sunxi_geth.c`. Verdict GREEN — self-contained designware-style drivers, the easiest high-value port (mostly DT/clock/EPHY plumbing).

4. **DRAM auto-scan** — not present as U-Boot source; it lives entirely in the SPL `.a` blobs (only `dram*.h` headers exist). RED — use mainline's parameterized SPL DRAM driver, treat the blob as a behavioral reference only.

Secure-boot/TOC, sprite, USB-efex and env are all YELLOW (GPL but bound to sunxi_flash/MBR) — port only if the factory workflow must be preserved. HDMI2.0 controller source was not found in `disp2/` — flagged UNVERIFIED.

## Chip support & out-of-tree harvest map (reports 08–11)

Base = official mainline v2025.07. Mainline is richer than first assumed: the
sunxi display driver files (`sunxi_de2.c`, `sunxi_lcd.c`, `lcdc.c`,
`sunxi_dw_hdmi.c`) and DRAM drivers (`dram_suniv.c`, `dram_sun20i_d1.c`) all
exist — but display is Kconfig-gated OFF for V3s/H3/suniv/T113/R528 (DE1 excludes
them; DE2 only A64/H6). Note: `sipeed_licheerv_nano` is Sophgo SG2002/CV1800B,
NOT Allwinner.

Per-chip:

| Chip | Mainline v2025.07 | Gaps | Out-of-tree harvest |
|---|---|---|---|
| H3 | mature (reference, many boards) | display | little needed; no good display source |
| V3s | mature (LicheePi Zero) | display, SPI-NAND | display: M. Cerveny DE2/TCON0 series (orphaned); SPI-NAND: adapt T113 work |
| F1C100s/200s | mature (licheepi_nano, lctech_pi) | RGB display, SPI-NAND | display: Lichee-Pi `nano-lcd800480`; SPI-NAND: Icenowy "suniv SPI NAND in SPL" |
| T113 | one shared board only | SPI-NAND, EMAC, display | SPI-NAND: Watts RFC (= our backport); EMAC: smaeul + vendor `sunxi_gmac`; display: vendor `disp2`/SyterKit |
| R528 | = T113 (sun8iw20) | same as T113 | same (evb2 already assembled here) |
| D1/D1s | drivers but NO board defconfig | defconfig, RISC-V SPL/OpenSBI | smaeul `d1-wip` (nezha/lichee_rv defconfig + OpenSBI + T-HEAD cache ops, absent in v2025.07) |
| R328 | absent entirely (sun8iw18) | everything | vendor `tina-r328` + YuzukiHD/YuzukiRosetta only |

Capability-level harvest + portability:

| Capability | Mainline | Best source | Portability |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPL SPI-NAND boot | none merged | Watts T113 RFC (backported), Icenowy suniv; vendor physical layer (GPL) | GREEN physical layer; vendor NFTL `nftl.S` = RED blob → use UBI/MTD |
| Display (TCON/DSI/RGB) | files present, gated off for these SoCs | vendor Tina `disp2` (TCON + MIPI-DSI + ~60 panel drivers, GPL) | YELLOW: port `disp_sys_intf` glue to mainline DM first, then panels ~mechanical (GREEN) |
| EMAC (T113/R528) | wired EMAC missing | vendor `sunxi_gmac.c` + smaeul gpio patch | GREEN — easiest high-value; needs EMAC_25M_CLK_REG fix |
| DRAM auto-scan | parameterized driver | vendor auto-scan lives in SPL `.a` blobs | RED — not portable; use mainline param driver, blob = behavioral ref |
| D1 RISC-V boot chain | no defconfig | smaeul `d1-wip` | GREEN — shares history, cherry-pickable (~1.5 yr behind) |

Honesty notes: local Lichee-Pi fork branches are 7–9-yr grafted snapshots
(reference only, everything is upstream now); both SPI-NAND RFCs are
unmerged/orphaned (SPI-NAND stays our own asset); some web sources were behind
Anubis (canonical URLs in report 10); exact per-chip display enablement to be
verified when the display phase starts.

## Next steps

- `sun8i-r528-evb2` target is assembled and builds (branch `mainline-evb2`).

131	NOT Allwinner.

135	| Chip | Mainline v2025.07 | Gaps | Out-of-tree harvest |
136	|---|---|---|---|
137	| H3 | mature (reference, many boards) | display | little needed; no good display source |

140	| T113 | one shared board only | SPI-NAND, EMAC, display | SPI-NAND: Watts RFC (= our backport); EMAC: smaeul + vendor `sunxi_gmac`; display: vendor `disp2`/SyterKit |
141	| R528 | = T113 (sun8iw20) | same as T113 | same (evb2 already assembled here) |
142	| D1/D1s | drivers but NO board defconfig | defconfig, RISC-V SPL/OpenSBI | smaeul `d1-wip` (nezha/lichee_rv defconfig + OpenSBI + T-HEAD cache ops, absent in v2025.07) |
143	| R328 | absent entirely (sun8iw18) | everything | vendor `tina-r328` + YuzukiHD/YuzukiRosetta only |
144	
145	Capability-level harvest + portability:
146	
147	| Capability | Mainline | Best source | Portability |
148	|---|---|---|---|
149	| SPL SPI-NAND boot | none merged | Watts T113 RFC (backported), Icenowy suniv; vendor physical layer (GPL) | GREEN physical layer; vendor NFTL `nftl.S` = RED blob → use UBI/MTD |
150	| Display (TCON/DSI/RGB) | files present, gated off for these SoCs | vendor Tina `disp2` (TCON + MIPI-DSI + ~60 panel drivers, GPL) | YELLOW: port `disp_sys_intf` glue to mainline DM first, then panels ~mechanical (GREEN) |
151	| EMAC (T113/R528) | wired EMAC missing | vendor `sunxi_gmac.c` + smaeul gpio patch | GREEN — easiest high-value; needs EMAC_25M_CLK_REG fix |
152	| DRAM auto-scan | parameterized driver | vendor auto-scan lives in SPL `.a` blobs | RED — not portable; use mainline param driver, blob = behavioral ref |
153	| D1 RISC-V boot chain | no defconfig | smaeul `d1-wip` | GREEN — shares history, cherry-pickable (~1.5 yr behind) |
154	
155	Honesty notes: local Lichee-Pi fork branches are 7–9-yr grafted snapshots
156	(reference only, everything is upstream now); both SPI-NAND RFCs are
157	unmerged/orphaned (SPI-NAND stays our own asset); some web sources were behind
158	Anubis (canonical URLs in report 10); exact per-chip display enablement to be
159	verified when the display phase starts.

169

172	- Do not run mainline checkouts in `~/mywork/u-boot` itself (dirty vendor tree);
173	  use worktrees under `~/mywork/uboot-wt/`.
174	- R328 (sun8iw18) is essentially unsupported in mainline — out of scope here.

# U-Boot Mainline Migration (Allwinner) — xstation

Sub-project of [embedded-dev](../README.md). This README is the global status
board; details are split into the sibling files.

## Identity

- Host: `xstation`
- Project: migrate Allwinner boards from vendor U-Boot 2018.07 (Tina SDK
  "brandy") to **mainline U-Boot v2025.07**, full-mainline boot chain, flashed
  via FEL (`xfel`) / SD.
- Working area: `~/mywork/uboot-wt/` (git worktrees off `~/mywork/u-boot`)
- Reports: `~/mywork/uboot-wt/_reports/01..` (markdown, per workstream) — kept in
  the worktree, referenced (not mirrored) here.
- Created record: 2026-05-25

## Documents in this sub-project

- [worktrees.md](worktrees.md) — U-Boot trees inventory, build environment,
  reference FEL bring-up commands
- [chip-support.md](chip-support.md) — chip support matrix & out-of-tree harvest
  map (reports 08–11)
- [spinand-backport.md](spinand-backport.md) — SPI-NAND SPL backport details
  (report 06)

## Goal / target chip set

Build one mainline-based U-Boot covering this Allwinner family. Mainline already
supports every SoC below; the per-target work is board DT + DRAM params +
console + boot media (NOT adding SoC support).

| Chip | Mainline MACH | Example defconfig | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| V3s | `MACH_SUN8I_V3S` | `LicheePi_Zero`, `pinecube` | sun8i, DDR |
| H3 | `MACH_SUN8I_H3` | `orangepi_*`, `nanopi_*` | broad upstream support |
| F1C100s/F1C200s | `MACH_SUNIV` | `licheepi_nano`, `lctech_pi_f1c200s` | suniv, ARM926, tiny RAM |
| T113 | `MACH_SUN8I_R528` (t113s) | `mangopi_mq_r` | sun8iw20, dual A7 |
| R528 | `MACH_SUN8I_R528` | `mangopi_mq_r` | sun8iw20, A7 + C906; same die as T113-s3 |

Mainline v2025.07 sunxi scope overall: ~70 defconfigs, ~157 DTs, families
sun4i/5i/6i/7i/8i/9i/suniv/sun50i/sun20i.

## Status (2026-05-25)

Done (non-hardware; all verified on disk):

- Mainline v2025.07 **builds for R528** (`mangopi_mq_r_defconfig`); artifacts
  `u-boot-sunxi-with-spl.bin` (~480 KB), `spl/sunxi-spl.bin` (valid `eGON.BT0`).
- **DRAM mapping** (report 02): T113/evb1 == upstream mangopi byte-for-byte;
  R528/evb2 = DDR3@792 via `CONFIG_DRAM_CLK=792` + DDR3 + ZQ `0x7b7bfb` +
  TPR0/11/12/13. Watch-item: R528/evb2 vendor sets `dram_tpr4=0x2000` (address
  muxing) which mainline forces to 0 with no override — prime suspect if R528
  DRAM training fails (would need a code change).
- **Board DT delta** (report 03): mainline `sun8i-t113s.dtsi` already has all
  controllers (disabled). evb2 needs UART0 console + SPI-NAND pins; display on
  evb2 is parallel RGB and mainline U-Boot has no sun20i display driver →
  display is Linux-only, omitted from the U-Boot DT.
- **SPI-NAND SPL backport** (report 06): branch `mainline-spinand`, compiles,
  boot path linked — details in [spinand-backport.md](spinand-backport.md).
- **xfel v1.3.3** built (`~/mywork/xfel/xfel`), supports R528/T113. Details in
  [worktrees.md](worktrees.md).
- **First per-board target assembled: `sun8i-r528-evb2`** (report 07): branch
  `mainline-evb2` (off `mainline-spinand`, commit `f657cecb`). New
  `configs/sun8i-r528-evb2_defconfig` + `arch/arm/dts/sun8i-r528-evb2.dts`.
  Builds (exit 0); UART0 console (PF2/PF4, `CONS_INDEX=1`), SPI-NAND boot
  (`SPL_SPI_SUNXI_NAND`, pagesize 0x800), evb2 DDR3@792 (`TPR11=0x450000`,
  `TPR12=0x34`), fixed regulators, USB host+OTG. Omitted: mmc0/mmc2 (pin
  conflicts) and parallel-RGB display. Artifact `u-boot-sunxi-with-spl.bin`
  (~533 KB).

Blocked on hardware (no FEL device attached at record time):

- FEL RAM bring-up, SD boot, and SPI-NAND on-target validation all need the
  board connected. SPI-NAND read correctness is unverified until then — see
  [spinand-backport.md](spinand-backport.md).

## Roadmap

# Chip support & out-of-tree harvest map (reports 08–11)

Base = official mainline U-Boot v2025.07. Mainline is richer than first assumed:
the sunxi display driver files (`sunxi_de2.c`, `sunxi_lcd.c`, `lcdc.c`,
`sunxi_dw_hdmi.c`) and DRAM drivers (`dram_suniv.c`, `dram_sun20i_d1.c`) all
exist — but display is Kconfig-gated OFF for V3s/H3/suniv/T113/R528 (DE1 excludes
them; DE2 only A64/H6). Note: `sipeed_licheerv_nano` is Sophgo SG2002/CV1800B,
NOT Allwinner.

## Per-chip

| Chip | Mainline v2025.07 | Gaps | Out-of-tree harvest |
|---|---|---|---|
| H3 | mature (reference, many boards) | display | little needed; no good display source |
| V3s | mature (LicheePi Zero) | display, SPI-NAND | display: M. Cerveny DE2/TCON0 series (orphaned); SPI-NAND: adapt T113 work |
| F1C100s/200s | mature (licheepi_nano, lctech_pi) | RGB display, SPI-NAND | display: Lichee-Pi `nano-lcd800480`; SPI-NAND: Icenowy "suniv SPI NAND in SPL" |
| T113 | one shared board only | SPI-NAND, EMAC, display | SPI-NAND: Watts RFC (= our backport); EMAC: smaeul + vendor `sunxi_gmac`; display: vendor `disp2`/SyterKit |
| R528 | = T113 (sun8iw20) | same as T113 | same (evb2 already assembled here) |
| D1/D1s | drivers but NO board defconfig | defconfig, RISC-V SPL/OpenSBI | smaeul `d1-wip` (nezha/lichee_rv defconfig + OpenSBI + T-HEAD cache ops, absent in v2025.07) |
| R328 | absent entirely (sun8iw18) | everything | vendor `tina-r328` + YuzukiHD/YuzukiRosetta only |

## Capability-level harvest + portability

| Capability | Mainline | Best source | Portability |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPL SPI-NAND boot | none merged | Watts T113 RFC (backported), Icenowy suniv; vendor physical layer (GPL) | GREEN physical layer; vendor NFTL `nftl.S` = RED blob → use UBI/MTD |
| Display (TCON/DSI/RGB) | files present, gated off for these SoCs | vendor Tina `disp2` (TCON + MIPI-DSI + ~60 panel drivers, GPL) | YELLOW: port `disp_sys_intf` glue to mainline DM first, then panels ~mechanical (GREEN) |
| EMAC (T113/R528) | wired EMAC missing | vendor `sunxi_gmac.c` + smaeul gpio patch | GREEN — easiest high-value; needs EMAC_25M_CLK_REG fix |
| DRAM auto-scan | parameterized driver | vendor auto-scan lives in SPL `.a` blobs | RED — not portable; use mainline param driver, blob = behavioral ref |
| D1 RISC-V boot chain | no defconfig | smaeul `d1-wip` | GREEN — shares history, cherry-pickable (~1.5 yr behind) |

## Honesty notes

- Local Lichee-Pi fork branches are 7–9-yr grafted snapshots (reference only,
  everything is upstream now).
- Both SPI-NAND RFCs (Watts / Icenowy) are unmerged/orphaned → SPI-NAND stays
  our own asset (see [spinand-backport.md](spinand-backport.md)).
- Some web sources were behind Anubis (canonical URLs in report 10).
- Exact per-chip display enablement to be verified when the display phase starts.

# SPI-NAND SPL boot backport (report 06)

The single biggest mainline gap for sun8iw20 (R528/T113) and the wider sunxi
family: mainline U-Boot SPL cannot boot from SPI-NAND. This backport closes it
in code. Full detail: `~/mywork/uboot-wt/_reports/06-spinand-backport.md`.

## What was done

- Branch `mainline-spinand` (off v2025.07), 2 commits:
  - `596b1820` — `SPL_SPI_SUNXI_NAND` + `SPL_SPI_SUNXI_NAND_ASSUMED_PAGESIZE`
    Kconfig and the `BOOT_DEVICE_SPINAND` boot path.
  - `9602fa40` — SPI-NAND page-read in `arch/arm/mach-sunxi/spl_spi_sunxi.c`:
    PAGE READ (0x13) → poll OIP via GET FEATURE (0x0F/0xC0) → READ FROM CACHE
    (0x03, 2-byte column) → RESET (0xFF); page-crossing logic; NAND-first /
    NOR-fallback; `BOOT_DEVICE_SPINAND` load method.
- Adapted to v2025.07 APIs (`spl_load_init`/`spl_load_simple_fit`,
  `struct legacy_img_hdr`, `CONFIG_TEXT_BASE`/`CONFIG_XPL_BUILD`,
  `ulong`-returning reader typedef). The FIFO reader was generalized to take a
  command + address width so one primitive serves both NOR and NAND.
- Because it edits the shared `spl_spi_sunxi.c`, it benefits **all sunxi SoCs**,
  not just R528/T113.

## Provenance (honest)

- Re-implemented from the **standard JEDEC SPI-NAND sequence**, not applied
  verbatim: the orphaned John Watts 2024 RFC ("Support SPI NAND booting on the
  T113", 15 patches, never merged) patch bodies could not be reproduced verbatim,
  and the smaeul `d1-wip` branch does not carry the code. Commits credit the
  originators; no fabricated Signed-off-by lines.

## Page-layout decision

- Mainline **physical** layout, 2 KiB pages (default), chip factory on-die ECC —
  NOT the BSP super-page/redundant layout. Flash with `xfel spinand` (matches),
  not a BSP image.

## Unverified until hardware is attached

1. Whether the BROM reports boot-media 3 (SPI) vs 1 (NAND) for SPI-NAND — kept on
   the SPI source with a documented fallback.
2. Page-read correctness / column-address width / dummy bytes.
3. OIP poll + reset timings.
4. On-die ECC default-enabled assumption.
5. Real page size.
6. End-to-end layout match (`xfel spinand` write vs SPL read).

## Proof it is linked (build-only)

- SPL grew ~18400 → ~19224 B when enabled; linker-list entry
  `..._BOOT_DEVICE_SPINAND0spl_spi_load_image` present; disassembly shows opcodes
  0x13/0x0F/0xC0/0xFF.
- In the `mainline-evb2` target, the SPL SPI-NAND path is gated by
  `SPL_SPI_SUNXI` only (dropped `SPL_SPI`/`CMD_SF`, which pulled DM
  `spi-sunxi.c` into SPL and needs `SPL_DM_SPI`).
